units.notes: The 2024 Resource Evaluation Study supports the capacity and the 2043 start year already in GEM, but names no site, turbine maker, or city. I found nothing newer that names this unit.

qa.recommendation: The August 2026 EIA-860M table has plant code 1048, Milton L Kapp, in Clinton County, about 2.9 km from GEM's coordinates. Generator 2 is 218.5 MW and generator 1 is 18.8 MW, both retired gas steam units. This placeholder is a future 466 MW turbine set for 2043, not a Kapp unit, so the codes should not be added here. The coordinates may simply sit on the old Kapp site. The reviewer should decide whether to keep them.
qa.note: The 2024 study names no site for this turbine. The Kapp retired units are a different kind of unit and capacity. I took the Kapp figures from the brief and did not re-read the EIA file.

source_log.note: MidAmerican's 2024 Resource Evaluation Study, filed November 2024, lists a 466 MW simple-cycle combustion turbine in 2043 in its preferred portfolio table. That matches GEM's start year of 2043. The study does not name a site, so this is an unsited placeholder. The plan is already cited for this unit, so there is nothing new to add.
